purpose: Teach: なべ/飼う/ちいさな/どら/通行人/お札/車道/絨毯

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、本気で、絶対、ばあさんの、絶対、なべ料理、絶対、お父さん、絶対、大好きだったぞ、覚えてる?本気で
lines.en: Gran, when you were young — you remember how much your father absolutely loved your nabe, don't you? I'm serious.
lines.style: Soft, nostalgic opening. Voice warm but searching — not quite asking, more inviting her into the memory. Gentle pace, each phrase a small caress of the past. Trails into the question like he's already seeing her face.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん。若い頃、本気で、絶対、家で、絶対、犬を、絶対、飼う、絶対、お祖父ちゃん、絶対、楽しみだったわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: Yes, I do. When I was young, your father was so looking forward to keeping a dog at home — remember that, dear? I'm serious about it.
lines.style: Bright recognition in the voice, then softening. A woman who loves that he remembers. Warm and present, not performing — just genuinely glad to be here in this moment with him. Speech unhurried, almost musical.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、ばあさんが、絶対、ちいさな、絶対、頃の写真、絶対、お父さん、絶対、宝物にしてたぞ、覚えてる?本気で
lines.en: When you were young — those photos of you as a tiny thing. Your father treasured them, remember? I'm serious.
lines.style: Voice catching slightly on the image of her as small. Reverent but unsentimental — just stating fact. Slower here. The kind of memory that sits heavy and good in the chest.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、本気で、絶対、若い頃、絶対、どら焼き、絶対、大好きだったわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: Your grandfather loved dorayaki so much when he was young, didn't he, dear? I remember it clearly.
lines.style: Warm laugh underneath the words, almost conspiratorial. She's alive in this memory — not recalling it but *being* in it for a moment. Gentle confirmation, like she's confirming something she's always known.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、町の、絶対、通行人、絶対、皆、絶対、知り合いだったぞ、ばあさん、覚えてる?本気で
lines.en: When you were young, everyone in town was someone we knew. Everyone, gran — remember that?
lines.style: A kind of amazement in the voice, almost wondering at it now. The pace slight slower on 'everyone' — letting the smallness of that world settle. Not quite wistful, but tender with recognition.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、お祖父ちゃんが、絶対、お札、絶対、初めて、絶対、稼いだ時、絶対、嬉しかったわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: When you were young, the day your grandfather earned his first real money — that made me so happy, remember? I do.
lines.style: Pride and quiet joy in her voice. The memory is still bright. She's not looking back — she's there. Steady pace, warm, no apology for the tenderness in it.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、車道、絶対、お父さん、絶対、自転車で、絶対、走り回っていたぞ、覚えてる、ばあさん?本気で
lines.en: When you were young, your father used to ride his bike up and down the street all the time. You remember that, don't you, gran?
lines.style: The image of movement in his voice — almost playful now, lighter than before. A flash of the boy he remembers. Quick pace on 'bike,' then settling. Like he's sharing something that still makes him smile.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 昔、本気で、絶対、ばあさんの、絶対、織りの、絶対、絨毯、絶対、お父さん、絶対、誇りにしていたわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: Long ago, your father was so proud of the carpet I wove — the one I made. You remember that, dear?
lines.style: Quiet pride, but softer now. Not boasting — just stating something true. Her voice contains both her hands at the loom and his face when he saw it. Slow, sure, the voice of someone who knows what matters.
